correctness.rationale: Independently write the character coordinates on D_+(z_12) as u_p/u_1, v_q/v_2 (p,q>=3), u_2/u_1 and v_1/v_2. These give all the stated ratio exponents, including e_a+e_b which are decomposable, and the generator differences span the entire indicated lattice. For X>=Y subtract Y copies of e_X+e_Y and allocate X-Y among the capacities b_q; for Y>=X swap the roles. This proves saturation and normality on an affine cover. The coordinate and two sum inequalities are the complete irredundant facet system: for each sum facet the opposite coordinate family, the corresponding mixed vectors and e_X+e_Y are independent of rank 2r+1; for a_p=0 take other coordinate generators and one e_X+e_b plus e_X+e_Y, and for X=0 take the coordinate a,b and one e_Y+e_a, with symmetric cases. All normals are primitive. The coordinate normal block is integral identity, so the cokernel is freely generated by the two noncoordinate divisors. The map to the local class group is onto; an invariant divisor in the kernel is Cartier near the fixed point, hence everywhere since the non-Cartier locus is invariant closed and every nonempty invariant closed subset contains the attracting fixed point. An invariant Cartier divisor on a single affine cone is principal. Subtracting the coordinate contributions to the canonical class by the all-ones character gives (r-1,r-1), with the stated sign convention K=-sum D. For r=1 this character has height one on all primitive normals, giving Gorenstein (not smooth); for r>=2 the class has infinite order. The 4r+1 generators have total coordinate weight 1 or 2, and the latter contain X or Y, absent from every sum of two weight-one vectors. Thus all are atoms and give the cotangent dimension. Every allowed edge supports a polytope vertex, e.g. by maximizing the two endpoint coordinates there, and label permutations are transitive.
